preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) representing the number of names.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(name) <= 100 for name in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the following n lines is a name (1 ≤ |name| ≤ 100) consisting only of lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: len({name for name in stdin.splitlines()[1:]}) == int(stdin.splitlines()[0])

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Impossible' or (len(stdout.strip()) == 26 and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in stdout.strip()) and len({c for c in stdout.strip()}) == 26)
postconditions.description: If no valid alphabet order exists, output is exactly 'Impossible'. Otherwise, output is a permutation of all 26 lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != 'Impossible' and all(compare_names(names[i], names[i+1], stdout.strip()) for i in range(len(names)-1))
postconditions.description: If a valid alphabet order exists, the output permutation ensures that the input names are sorted lexicographically under that order, where `compare_names` is defined as: for two names s and t, find the first differing character at position i (if any), and s < t iff the order of s[i] in the output permutation is less than the order of t[i]. If no differing character exists, the shorter name is considered smaller.
